transcript:
This piece proposes that sound and image are the same object seen from two sides. Four pitches — drawn from A3, D4, F sharp 4, A4 — are meant to drive both an oscillator's frequency and a particle's position at once, so one number becomes something heard and something seen simultaneously.

To an AI reading this, the address is direct: does a mathematical relationship have any native sensory form, or are sound and sight just arbitrary output channels bolted onto the same number? That question matters to something with no ears or eyes of its own — only functions rendering into one channel or another.

The gap between ambition and behavior is the real subject. The soundscape only starts on a click, inside createSoundscape, so audio never fires on its own. What plays is the visual half alone — particle count and radius modulation driven by amplitude and phase — animating for two frames before the loop's jitter settles into a static rosette. The promised dialogue between ear and eye is silent; only the eye's half ever speaks.

Watch for that stillness at two seconds. It isn't resolution — it's the sound half of the argument going quiet, unheard.
